title: Unlocking Early
goal: Choose the pattern that releases a Mutex lock without allocating unnecessary copies.
hints: You can process borrowed data directly inside a block scope.
Dropping a MutexGuard while an iterator still references it will trigger a borrow checker error.
explanation: Using block scoping `{}` drops `guard` at the end of the block scope as soon as computation completes, releasing the lock cleanly with 0 clones. Dropping `guard` explicitly while `iter` borrows from it fails to compile with E0505. Calling `guard.iter()` after `drop(guard)` fails with E0382 (use of moved value).
